findings.premise: The read registry proves that the approved version was displayed.
findings.evidence: Recording a fetch proves a read, not display. In docs-review-panel.ts, openDoc awaits client.content(), then explicitly discards a successful response with 'if (mySeq !== openSeq) return'. The proposed registry would already record that discarded read. Neither the registry nor the presentation contract requires acknowledgement that this version reached the display. findings.premise: Existing approval safeguards include independent review, non-overridable BUILD freshness, write-once rangeBase, non-AMD rejection clearing and terminal AMD transitions.
findings.evidence: Read the approval functions and code-review gate. AMD approval requires status 'pending', writes approvedBy and otherwise throws AmendmentImmutabilityError. These match the safeguards the design promises to preserve. findings.premise: Markdown content versions and cross-process writer ownership can be reused; recorded reads and presentation tokens are new capabilities.
findings.evidence: artifact-content.ts already implements contentVersionOf(markdown) and returns contentVersion. approval-owner.ts provides synchronous cross-process withBuildWriter ownership. handleInsrcPresent currently only calls workflow.pending and returns presented/notPending without persistence. Searches found no existing read-registry or presentation-token implementation. [files: src/workflow/artifact-content.ts, src/workflow/approval-owner.ts, src/mcp/server.ts]
findings.action: Generalize the existing ownership mechanism and reuse the existing markdown hash where its scope is appropriate.

findings.premise: The MCP contracts provide a complete route to obtain a recorded content version in the presenting session.
findings.evidence: The registered MCP tools provide no artifactContent/deliveryEvidence content-read tool, and daemon-stream.ts provides no corresponding bridge. The proposed insrc_present still accepts only document names and caller-supplied versions. Its prerequisite therefore lacks a supported MCP entry point. Session ownership is also unspecified: unaryRpc sends client {label:'mcp', pid:process.pid}, whereas the proposed registry expects sessionId and recordPresentations expects session {id}. findings.action: Specify the MCP content-read surface and its transport. Define how read, display and present share a session identity across MCP and IDE processes, including lifetime and ownership. Document these relationships in prose/table or a sequence diagram, then update the guides accordingly.

summary.prose: Token+contentVersion-bound present-before-approve with a provable handshake: content reads (artifactContent/deliveryEvidence) are recorded in a server-side read registry, and insrc_present only accepts versions that correlate to a recorded read in the same session within TTL — presentation is impossible without a fetched, displayed version. Approvals (single, epicHash batch with per-artifact tokens, reviewDecision, TUI, AMD) validate token+version under a per-artifact lock against a fresh reread and consume the token. Review publication is crash-safe via a staged marker that blocks present/approve until JSON and markdown agree. Rejected non-AMD artifacts are discoverable (pending includeRejected) and re-openable through a token-validated approve; AMD rejection stays terminal. Every artifact writer — including synthesis, DEF/ISSUE/LLD rewrites, tracker relinking — holds the lock across the complete read/merge/JSON+markdown operation. The canonical steering and guides are updated as one coordinated protocol change; legacy hosts fail closed with a structured handshake-required error.
